tocPath: APPROACH TO PATIENTS WITH EMERGENCY CONDITIONS
The Concept of Emergency Care and Resuscitation

blocks.text: Perform the primary and secondary assessment with interventions when needed.
For generalized pain give analgesics, advise the patient to rest and make a follow-up. For joint, infections, injury, eye and ear pains treat as for main disease.

Fever is an abnormal elevation of body temperature that occurs as part of a specific biologic response that is mediated and controlled by the central nervous system and is usually a symptom of an infection. It is characterized by an elevation of body temperature above the normal range of 36.5–37.5 0C

blocks.text: Airway: Protect as appropriate and ensure Cervical-spine immobilization.

It refers to the loss of body water, with or without salt at a rate greater than the body can replace it. The cause of dehydration is a combination of physiological and disease processes. Persons at greatest risk for dehydration include persons with diarrhoea, vomiting, fever, diabetes or infections, impaired level status.

blocks.text: Perform both primary and secondary assessments and provide the necessary interventions.
Give oxygen if hypoxic or increased work of breathing
Put TWO large-bore IV cannulas for fluid resuscitations
The treatment for minor dehydration, often considered the most effective, is drinking water and stopping fluid loss.
In more severe cases, correction of a dehydrated state is accomplished by the replenishment of necessary water and electrolytes.
